answers.answer: Each player takes twelve ordinary turns: the 16 spaces are four seasons of three ordinary rounds plus a courtship. Courtship has no player turns, service rotation, monument income, or Servants’ Hall use.
answers.evidence: Overview: ‘each player takes twelve ordinary turns. Courtship is an event, with no player turns, service rotation, monument income or Servants’ Hall use.’

answers.answer: Hosting order: (1) move servants from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service, then Expended Service to Servants’ Quarters (each advances one space; do not move expended servants twice); (2) resolve the round-track event, then applicable monument and Servants’ Hall effects in either order; (3) choose an activity tile; (4) invite the exact required gentry; (5) provide required service; (6) take favours, all positive before all negative; (7) optionally buy one improvement; (8) clear: all used servants to Expended Service, played gentry to the personal discard pile, and return the activity tile to its tableau column, flipping/upgrading as required. The last player advances the round marker.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Hosting an activity steps 1–8: ‘Check round track, then ongoing tiles’; cleanup sends servants to Expended Service, gentry to personal discard, and returns the tile to its tableau column.

answers.answer: Pass order: all servants directly to Available Service; all gentry in your discard to hand; resolve the round-track event, then ongoing tile effects; choose either £200 or a free Market refresh; optionally buy one tile. Any servant used for an ongoing effect is expended at turn end. Butler’s Room hiring is an activity, not a passing benefit, so you cannot hire through it as a pass benefit.
answers.evidence: Passing: ‘all servants directly to Available Service → all gentry in your discard to hand → round-track event, then ongoing tile effects → choose £200 or a free Market refresh → optional one tile purchase’; Butler’s Room hiring is an activity.

answers.answer: Yes. The PR screen is fixed at the end of step 2, before choosing the activity, so reputation level 6.1 is used to check the PR6 tile and guests. The four Service Help actions may then lower actual reputation to 3.4 without invalidating the activity. Each costs three reputation increments and moves one servant from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service; it cannot take a servant directly from Expended Service. The action is legal as described, since special actions may lower actual reputation after screening.
answers.evidence: Reputation screening: ‘fixed at the end of step 2, before Choose Activity’ and special actions later ‘may lower actual reputation below those PRs without invalidating the activity.’ Service Help moves one servant from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service.

answers.answer: Resolve all positive favours before all negative favours; choose any order within those groups. At minimum reputation, you cannot take a negative reputation favour first to avoid the loss. A money penalty must be fully payable: use positive money favours, a money VP card, or Borrow Money; if short, borrow if possible, otherwise you cannot play that guest/tile.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 6 requires positive favours before negative. Special Rules: ‘You cannot take a negative favour first to shelter it at minimum reputation’; money penalty must be fully payable.

answers.answer: Borrow Money: lose 2 reputation increments, gain £100; repeatable. Service Help: lose 3 increments, move one servant from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service; repeatable. Refresh Market: lose 4 increments and fully refresh the Market; this special action is limited to once per turn. At minimum reputation you cannot take a special action. Service Help cannot take a servant directly from Expended Service.
answers.evidence: Special-action table lists all three costs/effects and limits; reputation section says ‘At minimum you cannot ... take a special action.’

answers.answer: Host the Butler’s Room with an available butler or underbutler and no gentry. Take up to two servants from Servants for Hire, excluding underbutlers, into Expended Service; there is no money fee. On first use, the room upgrades. Its upgraded side instead lets you recruit one common servant (footman, valet, or lady’s maid) from any location on one opponent’s family board into your Expended Service, rather than hiring up to two from the supply. Unique servants cannot be recruited.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring, Butler’s Room: ‘no gentry’; hires up to two non-underbutlers from supply into Expended Service; upgraded room recruits one common servant from an opponent board.

answers.answer: A housekeeper may substitute for a lady’s maid only when no lady’s maids are available. With a Brushing Room in your tableau, footmen may substitute for valets only when no valets are available. An underbutler may substitute for any base male servant (butler, valet, or footman), even if that regular type is still available.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring: housekeeper and footman substitutions are conditional on no regular servant being available; underbutler may substitute even when that type remains available.

answers.answer: The only way to acquire an underbutler is purchasing Butler’s Pantry; take it from supply immediately into Expended Service. It is not immediately available: normally it moves to Servants’ Quarters at your next service rotation, then to Available Service at your second subsequent rotation. Passing or a Refresh Service VP card can make it available earlier; once in Quarters, Service Help or the Servants’ Quarters tile can permit earlier use. Another player cannot recruit it through Butler’s Room or a Hire Servant VP card; those methods exclude underbutlers.
answers.evidence: Butler’s Pantry is ‘the only way to acquire an underbutler’; hire methods explicitly exclude underbutlers; the summary gives its Expended-to-Quarters-to-Available timing.

answers.answer: In the Market, pay the market-space price plus the tile’s printed price modifier. In Reserve, the base price is £300 plus the modifier. The price cannot be below £100. You may never acquire a duplicate tile you already own, but reputation does not restrict purchasing, so you may buy a tile above your reputation.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve: Market-space price plus modifier; Reserve base £300 plus modifier; minimum £100; never acquire a duplicate; PR does not restrict purchasing.

answers.answer: When a Market space empties, slide remaining tiles left and draw replacements into the rightmost spaces. Stack a drawn duplicate on its matching Market tile and draw again; duplicates share one space and its price. If a drawn tile qualifies for Reserve, send it straight to Reserve and draw again. When filling multiple spaces, sort only newly drawn tiles by ascending sorting number. Buying one tile from a two-tile duplicate stack leaves the space occupied, so it causes no refill.
answers.evidence: Refill: ‘slide remaining tiles left’; stack duplicates and draw again; Reserve-eligible tiles go straight to Reserve; sort only new tiles. Buying one from a stack leaves an occupied space.

answers.answer: After courtship 1, move all Market Service tiles except Largest Wine Cellar to Reserve; later Service draws also go directly there, with that same exception. After courtship 2, also move all Market PR1 tiles to Reserve, and later PR1 draws go there. Largest Wine Cellar never enters Reserve. After each of the first three courtships, fully refresh the Market after Reserve movement: set all Market tiles aside, refill the six spaces under normal rules, then return the set-aside tiles to the bag and mix. This full seasonal refresh is standard in this scope.
answers.evidence: Open Reserve and Refresh sections specify post-courtship moves and exceptions; ‘Full refresh occurs after each of the first three courtships’; overview says full seasonal refresh is standard.

answers.answer: At each courtship, first return both Fairchilds to Alderley Hall. In courtships 1–3, score the current theme’s tile VP, including negatives; only the face-up hybrid category counts. The highest score wins one VP card and chooses one Fairchild for hand. On a tie for highest, each tied player draws one VP card and no Fairchild is awarded. Every player discards one secret objective; shuffle the discards together and put them face down on the bottom of the objective deck. After the first three courtships, pass the first-player marker anticlockwise (as part of seasonal upkeep).
answers.evidence: Courtship and seasonal upkeep: both Fairchilds return first; current theme score/tie handling, objective discards, and anticlockwise first-player pass are specified.

answers.answer: Final courtship scores tile VP across all four revealed themes; repeated categories count each time, including negative VP. The highest gets one VP card and a Fairchild. A tie is broken by highest reputation level, ignoring wheel position; if still tied, no Fairchild is awarded and tied winners draw VP cards under the tie rule. Players discard the final objective, then have a final chance to use special actions and VP cards for benefits where possible before scoring. Only a Fairchild won in final courtship retains its 8 VP for final scoring.
answers.evidence: Final courtship section specifies all four themes, tie process, final objective discard, last chance for special actions/VP cards, and Fairchild scoring.

answers.answer: End-game VP categories: improvement tiles (all face-up printed VP, including negatives and unused tiles); gentry in hand and discard (including negatives, family, and final Fairchild; dismissed guests do not score); fulfilled objectives; reputation; servants (2 VP each); wealth (1 VP per £200, rounded down); and retained unused VP cards (printed VP). Reputation levels 1–7 score 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, and 28 VP, respectively. Victory tiebreaks: player with final Fairchild wins; otherwise highest reputation level wins; otherwise share victory. Wheel position never breaks the game tie.
answers.evidence: Final VP table lists scoring categories and reputation values; tiebreak paragraph gives final Fairchild, reputation level, then shared victory.

answers.answer: Normally each player gets five objectives at setup and two more on round 6. Each player discards one at each of four courtships, leaving three to score; extra objectives from Main Library or a VP card increase the retained final count without an extra discard. Simultaneous discards are shuffled together, then put face down on the bottom of the objective deck. Tile objectives require owning the named tiles at game end, not upgrading them.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards: ‘five at setup plus two on round 6’; discard one at each of four courtships, leaving three; simultaneous discards shuffled; tile objective does not require upgraded tiles.

answers.answer: A VP card may be used immediately when drawn, at any time on your own later turn (several may be used), and once more after final courtship before scoring. Reveal it and discard it for its benefit; used cards go to the bottom of the VP deck. Retained cards stay hidden with objectives and score their printed VP at game end; you cannot take both benefit and final VP.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards section gives use timing, bottom-deck destination, retained-card scoring, and the mutually exclusive benefit/VP choice.

answers.answer: A normal activity tile must flip to its rose/upgrade side after its first use; an already-upgraded normal tile remains on that side after later uses. A hybrid starts with its underlined category icon showing, flips after every use, and moves to the newly face-up category. An activity tile that upgrades into an ongoing monument hosts its front-side activity once, then upgrades and cannot host again; its monument benefit begins on later turns. Only the currently face-up hybrid category counts for courtship and objectives.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects: normal tiles upgrade after first use; hybrids flip each use and count by face-up category; Queen’s and Lionheart Suites upgrade into monuments and cannot host again.

answers.answer: On a hosting turn, resolve the round event first, then applicable monument and Servants’ Hall effects during ongoing effects step 2; on a pass, recover all servants and gentry first, then resolve event and ongoing effects at step 3. Monuments give one reputation per ordinary turn, hosting or passing, but no courtship income; a newly purchased monument first pays on a later turn. Servants’ Hall uses one available servant during its effect: place that servant on the tile to lower one opponent’s reputation by one and gain one reputation yourself; the servant cannot also serve the activity and is expended at turn end. You cannot target a player at minimum reputation.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure places ongoing effects after the event on hosting and after recovery on passing. Monuments and Servants’ Hall paragraphs specify income, servant use, destination, and minimum-reputation restriction.

answers.answer: Heritage Guest Suite: put one footman on the tile and play one casual guest from hand; provide that guest’s normal service. Double all the guest’s favours, including negative ones; it upgrades and remains an activity tile. Queen’s Suite: put a housekeeper on the tile and play one prestige guest from hand; provide normal guest service. Double one chosen favour and resolve the others normally; it upgrades into a monument. Lionheart Suite: put a butler on the tile and draw one prestige guest from the deck to attend, with no personal guest service; double nonnegative favours, excluding negative favours from doubling, keep the guest and place it in discard at cleanup; it upgrades into a monument. Each suite has a fixed count of one guest, which cannot be increased or decreased.
answers.evidence: Suite table specifies each guest source, tile service, guest service, doubling rule and later tile state; following text says all have a fixed count of one guest and no effect changes it.
